name: gantt — Round Robin, one lane
note: Blocks are {p, from, to}. Use p:'idle' for CPU idle time. arrivals draw ▲ markers; marks draw dashed vertical lines.

spec.title: Round Robin, q = 4
spec.caption: P1 (burst 5) is preempted at t = 4 and queues behind P2 and P3, which arrived while it ran.

name: gantt — one lane per process
note: lanes:'by-process' shows waiting at a glance.

name: graph — DFA (manual layout)
note: shape: circle | double (accepting) | square | diamond | none. start:true draws the entry arrow. Parallel opposite edges curve automatically; self-loops are drawn above the node.

spec.title: Strings over {0,1} with an even number of 1s

name: graph — process state diagram
note: Use fill:'a'..'h' to colour nodes, style:'dashed' for dashed edges, curve to bend an edge.

name: graph — resource-allocation graph (circle layout)
note: layout:'circle' places nodes automatically; 'layers' draws a DAG top-down.

spec.title: Resource-allocation graph
spec.caption: A cycle with single-instance resources means deadlock.

name: tree — binary search tree
note: children: [] in order; use null for a missing left/right child when binary:true. highlight lists labels to colour.

name: table — page-replacement trace
note: Plain HTML table. cells: {"row,col": "a|b|c|d|ok|bad|hl|mute"} colours a cell. rowLabels:true makes column 0 a header.

name: memory — process address space
note: Vertical stack of boxes. size is a relative height. addr labels the top edge. brackets group rows.

name: memory — contiguous allocation (horizontal)
note: orientation:'h' lays blocks left to right; kind:'hole' draws a hatched free block.

brackets.label: total free = 400 K, but the largest hole is only 300 K (external fragmentation)

name: seq — sequence of events across lanes
note: events: {lane,text,kind:'op|block|ok|bad'} for a box on a lane; {from,to,text} for an arrow; {note,over:[lanes]} for a spanning note. Optional laneColors: {"Lane":"a".."h"} (or an array) colours each lane and its boxes and arrows; default is by position.

name: layers — protocol stack
note: Top to bottom. side draws a labelled vertical arrow (arrow:'down'|'up').

name: bits — header layout
note: fields wrap across rows of `width` bits. sub gives a small second line. Optional "msb":true numbers the bits from the right (leftmost = width-1), labels centred on each bit, for address lines and register bit positions.

name: flow — flowchart
note: kinds: start | end | process | decision | io. Edges are [from, to, label]. Back edges (loops) are routed around the right side.

nodes.label: Pick next process from ready queue

name: plot — growth rates
note: fn is a safe expression in x (+ - * / ^, sin cos log log2 ln exp sqrt abs min max floor ceil, pi e). pts:[[x,y],…] draws raw points. points:[{x,y,label}] marks dots.

name: array — pointers over cells
note: cells may be numbers or {v, hl:'a'..'h'}. pointers: [{at, label, color}].

name: kmap — four variables, corner group
note: vars: 2–5 names, first = most significant bit ("ABCD" or ["x1","x2","x3"]). Values from m (minterms → 1), d (don't-cares → X), M (maxterms → 0, the rest 1) or grid (rows top to bottom in the map's Gray order, e.g. ["1001","0110",…], 0/1/X). groups: {term:"B'D'"} or {cells:[0,2,8,10]}, plus color a–h and label (defaults to the term, else the term is worked out from the cells). Groups wrap round the edges and the four corners by themselves; a group that is not a rectangle of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 adjacent cells, or that mixes 1s and 0s, is an error ("wrong": true draws a deliberately wrong group, dashed). index:true prints the minterm number in each cell; hl:[5,7] or {"5":"bad"} tints cells; zeros:false hides the 0s; split:1 puts one variable on the rows; cell: cell size in px (44); legend: false or "below".

spec.title: f(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15)
spec.caption: The four corners are adjacent (the map wraps both ways), so they form one group, B'D'. f = B'D' + BD.

name: kmap — POS: grouping 0s, with a don't-care
note: A sum term in brackets, "(C)" or "(A' + B)", groups 0s (POS); when every group is a sum term the 0s are drawn bold and the 1s faint. Here the values are given as a grid (rows A = 0, A = 1; columns BC = 00, 01, 11, 10).

spec.title: F(A,B,C) = ΠM(0, 2, 4, 5) + d(6)
spec.caption: The 0-group (C) wraps from the left edge to the right edge and uses the don't-care at 6. F = C · (A' + B).

name: kmap — five variables as two maps
note: Five variables draw as two 4-variable maps side by side, A = 0 and A = 1 (the first variable picks the map; minterm = 16·A + the 4-variable index). A group whose term does not mention A is drawn in both maps. With five variables the legend goes below.

spec.title: f = Σm(0, 2, 5, 8, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26, 29, 31)
spec.caption: C'E' is the four corners of both maps; CD'E is the same column pair in both maps. f = C'E' + CD'E + ABCE.

name: circuit — two-level NAND–NAND, input bus, highlighted path
note: parts: {id, kind, at:[column, row]} on a grid of grid:[70,46] px per column/row (fractions allowed; a pin such as "g1.2" in place of a number lines the part up with that pin). Gates: and, or, not, nand, nor, xor, xnor, buf; n = inputs (2); input pins g1.1 … g1.n top to bottom, output g1.y (or just g1); neg:[1,3] adds inversion bubbles on inputs, neg:["y"] on the output; label writes a small name inside. Terminals: kind in / out, side = where the wire attaches (in: r, out: l; t/b for lines from above or below), label ("~A" draws A with a bar). wires: ["A","g1.1"] or {from, to (a pin or a list = fan-out sharing one trunk), x: trunk column, y: detour row, via:[[c,r],…] waypoints, label, labelAt:[c,r], color, dash}. Routing is orthogonal; trunks of different nets in the same gap are spread apart automatically; a dot marks a junction of one net, crossing nets get no dot. path:["B","g2","g4","F"] colours those parts and the wires between consecutive ones (pathColor, default bad); color on a part or wire colours just that one.

spec.title: Majority function, NAND–NAND
spec.caption: F = AB + BC + CA. Each input drops down a vertical line; a dot marks where it branches, and lines that merely cross have no dot. The highlighted path B → g2 → g4 → F is two gate delays.

name: circuit — MUX tree with a routed select line
note: mux: n = 2, 4, 8 or 16 data inputs d0, d1, … (top to bottom), select pins on the slanted bottom edge, most significant on the left (s1, s0; a 2:1 mux's is s), output y; en:true adds an enable pin on top. S0 reaches the upper mux through via waypoints; the two S0 wires form one net, so the split gets a dot.

spec.title: 4:1 MUX from three 2:1 MUXes
spec.caption: S1 S0 = 10 selects I2: the lower mux passes I2 (S0 = 0) and the right mux takes its input 1 (S1 = 1).

name: circuit — 4-bit ripple-carry adder
note: Blocks: fa (a, b, cin → s, cout; chain:true puts a, b on top, s below, cout left, cin right, for ripple chains drawn MSB first), ha (a, b → s, c), dec (n inputs a(n−1) … a0 → y0 …; en:true), enc (n inputs i0 … → y…; valid:true adds v), box (pins:{l:[…], r:[…], t:[…], b:[…]}, label, optional size:[w,h]; a pin written "op:F" is called op and labelled F). Terminals above the blocks use side:"b", those below side:"t", and line up with pins through at:["fa3.a", -0.2]. Wire labels go where they clear other wires, or at labelAt.

spec.title: 4-bit ripple-carry adder
spec.caption: The carry ripples right to left through all four stages (highlighted), so the sum is ready only after c3 settles.

name: circuit — synchronous counter sharing one clock
note: Flip-flops: dff (d), tff (t), jkff (j, k), srff (s, r), each with clk (drawn as the clock triangle), q and qn (Q̄). pre:true / clr:true add PRE on top and CLR below; neg:["pre","clr"] makes them active-low; edge:"neg" puts a bubble on the clock (falling-edge triggered). The clock is one wire per flip-flop with x = the column of its riser, so each riser sits just left of its clock pin and the shared line gets dots.

spec.title: 3-bit synchronous counter (T flip-flops)
spec.caption: T0 = 1, T1 = Q0, T2 = Q0·Q1: a flip-flop toggles when every lower bit is 1. All three share one clock.

name: circuit — every part kind
note: A visual index of the kinds (no wires): and, or, xor, not, nand, nor, xnor, buf, or with neg:[1,2], dff with pre/clr, jkff with edge:"neg", dec, enc, mux n:4, and a box. Pin names are shown inside the blocks.

spec.title: Every part kind
spec.caption: Gates and, or, xor, not; nand (n = 3), nor (n = 4), xnor, buf; or with bubbled inputs, D flip-flop with active-low PRE/CLR, JK on the falling edge; dec, enc, 4:1 mux, a generic box.

name: wave — counter waveforms, clock with edge marks
note: lanes: {name, clk: period in time units, phase: time of the first rising edge (0), inv:true starts with the low half, edges: "rise" | "fall" | "both" draws arrows on the edges}; {name, bits: "0110x1z"} with one character per time unit: 0, 1, x (unknown, hatched), z (high impedance, middle line), . (same as before); {gap:true} adds a little space. Every lane spans the same time (t, default the longest string; a shorter lane holds its last value). unit: px per time unit (auto); grid: n or {step, from} draws faint lines; marks: [{t, label, color}] dashed vertical lines across all lanes; color on a lane colours its line. Names may use ~ for a bar: "~Q", "F = A·~B", "~{A+B}".

spec.title: 3-bit synchronous up counter
spec.caption: Q0 toggles on every rising edge, Q1 on edges where Q0 was 1, Q2 on edges where Q1 and Q0 were both 1. The count bus reads Q2 Q1 Q0.

name: wave — gate delays and a glitch
note: arrows: [{from:[lane, time], to:[lane, time], label, color}] with lanes by name or index. Between lanes the arrow points from one edge to the edge it causes (delays); within one lane it becomes a dimension arrow under the lane (periods, pulse widths). axis: true or {step, scale, from, unit} prints times under the lanes (label = from + t × scale).

spec.title: Static-0 hazard: A·A' glitches for one inverter delay
spec.caption: F should stay 0, but for 1 ns both inputs of the AND are 1: the NOT gate is still catching up.

name: wave — bus values, unknown and high-impedance
note: bus: "x=..=.z" with data:["0x3F", …]: = starts the next value from data, 2–9 start a coloured value (2 = a … 9 = h), x is unknown (hatched), z high impedance, . continues. A value too long for its segment is shrunk, then hidden (it stays in the hover title). The T lane shows a same-lane arrow measuring one clock period.

spec.title: Read cycle
spec.caption: The address is valid from the first rising edge; data appears on the bus one access time later and the bus floats (z) otherwise.

name: shapes — geometry: polygon, angles, dimensions
note: items are drawn in order; coordinates are user units with y pointing up, and the figure scales to fit (u: px per unit, default 40; w: max width, 560). Kinds: poly {pts, v: vertex labels}, rect {at: lower-left corner, w, h, r: corner radius, v}, circle {c, r}, ellipse {c, rx, ry}, arc {c, r, a: [from°, to°] counter-clockwise from +x, sector: true closes it to the centre}, line {pts, arrow: "end" | "start" | "both"}, text {at, t, size (13), anchor, weight, color}. Style keys on any shape: fill (a–h, a light tint), solid: true (full colour), hatch: true, color (outline), dash: true (fold lines), width (px). angle {at: vertex, from, to: a point on each arm, r: radius in px (18), label, right: true for the square mark, reflex: true}. dim {from, to, label, off: distance from the segment in units, positive = left of from → to}.

spec.title: Triangle with an angle, a right angle and dimensions
spec.caption: Right angle at A; θ is the angle at B, so tan θ = 3/4.

name: shapes — figure, rotated, mirrored (groups and transforms)
note: group {items, tf, id}; use {ref: a group id, tf} draws that group again. tf is a list applied in order: ["translate", dx, dy], ["rotate", deg, [cx, cy]] (counter-clockwise, centre optional), ["scale", s] or ["scale", sx, sy] or ["scale", s, [cx, cy]], ["mirror", "v", x] (in the vertical line through x), ["mirror", "h", y], ["mirror", [x1, y1], [x2, y2]]. def: true on a group defines it without drawing it.

spec.title: Rotate, then mirror
spec.caption: The second figure is the first turned 90° clockwise; the third is the second reflected in the dashed line.

name: shapes — cube stacks, a cut cube and dice
note: cubes {h: rows of stack heights, back row first, each row left to right; or cells: [[x, y, z] or [x, y, z, colour], …]; at: where the origin cube sits; size; color} draws an isometric stack with shaded faces (hidden faces are skipped). cube {at, size, n: cuts per edge, color} is one big cube cut n × n × n (painted-cube questions). die {n: 1–6, at: centre, size} is a flat die face; die {iso: [top, left, right]} is a die in 3-D: numbers become pips, other text is written on the face.

spec.title: Count the cubes
spec.caption: Left: stacks of heights 3, 2, 1 / 2, 1, 1 / 1, 1, 0 (back row first) — 12 cubes. Middle: a cube cut into 27. Right: dice.

name: shapes — cube net, dotted paper, hatching
note: net {cells: [[column, row], …] with row 0 at the top, labels and fills per cell, fill for all, at: top-left corner, size, grid: true draws squared paper around it, fold: true dashes the shared (fold) edges}. grid {x: [from, to], y: [from, to], step, dots: true} draws squared or dotted paper anywhere. Also shown: a hatched polygon, an arc with an arrowhead, a dashed ellipse, a sector and a rounded rectangle.

spec.title: A cube net on a square grid
spec.caption: Fold lines are dashed. Faces 1 and 6, 2 and 4, 3 and 5 end up opposite each other.

name: shapes — mirror image of text
note: Labels stay upright under transforms, unless the text item has flip: true: then the letters are mirrored or rotated with their group, as needed for mirror-image questions.

spec.title: Mirror image of a word

items.t: its mirror image (mirror on the dashed line)

spec.caption: Text in a group with flip:true is mirrored with it; ordinary labels stay upright.

name: venn — two sets with probabilities, one region shaded
note: sets: 2 or 3 names; universe: true or its label ("U", "S") draws the box. Regions are named by set expressions: & (and, ∩), | (or, ∪), - (minus), ! or a trailing ' (complement), brackets, and U for everything. regions: {expression: text} writes text in one piece each, e.g. "A&!B" (only A), "A&B", "!(A|B)" (outside both); the text goes where it has the most room and never overlaps. shade: [expressions] in color (default a), or {expression: colour, …}; hatch: true hatches instead of tinting. colors: [colour per set outline]; r: circle radius in px.

name: venn — three sets with counts and coloured outlines
note: With three sets each labelled piece names all three: "Cricket&Football&!Hockey" is the only-those-two piece; a label whose expression covers two or more pieces is an error. Long set names are fine. A region value can also be {t, color}.

spec.title: Survey of 100 students
spec.caption: Exactly two sports (shaded): 11 + 7 + 6 = 24 students. The eight numbers add up to 100.

name: venn — a shaded expression, hatched
note: shade takes any expression and fills every piece it covers: here (A ∪ B)' ∩ C, written "(A|B)'&C".

spec.title: (A ∪ B)' ∩ C, hatched
spec.caption: Inside C but outside both A and B.

name: venn — no universe box
note: Without universe the circles stand alone; the outside piece can still be labelled.

name: plot — bars (pmf / histogram) with value labels and explicit ticks
note: A series with bars: true draws vertical bars at each point's x instead of a line; bw: bar width in x units (default 0.6 × the closest spacing; use the bin width for a histogram); values: true writes the value above each bar (a third entry in a point, [x, y, "1/16"], replaces the number). xticks / yticks: explicit tick values, numbers or [value, "label"] pairs, instead of the automatic ones. Plots without these keys are unchanged.

spec.title: Binomial(4, 1/2): P(X = k)
spec.caption: Bars sit on the x-axis at each k; values:true writes each bar's value (here the third entry of each point, a fraction).

name: plot — area under a curve between two x values
note: areas: [{under: series number or an expression such as "exp(-x)", from, to, color (default the series colour), label (written at the area's centre), hatch: true}] shades between the curve and the x-axis over [from, to] (default the whole x range).

spec.title: Standard normal: P(−1 < Z < 1)
spec.caption: The shaded area under the density between −1 and 1 is the probability, about 0.683.

name: plot — area between two curves
note: areas: [{between: [i, j], from, to, …}] shades between series i (above) and series j.

spec.title: Area between y = x and y = x²
spec.caption: ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6.

name: plot — a 2-D region (the meeting problem)
note: regions: [{pts: [[x, y], …] in data coordinates, color, label, hatch: true, outline: true, dash: true, fill: false}] fills any polygon, e.g. the band |x − y| ≤ 15 inside the 60 × 60 square; a second region with fill:false, outline:true draws the square. Make w and h match for a square plot area.

spec.title: Meeting problem: |x − y| ≤ 15
spec.caption: They meet when the arrival times differ by at most 15 minutes: 1 − (45/60)² = 7/16 of the square.

name: tree — probability tree with edge labels
note: edge on a node labels the edge coming into it from its parent (branch probabilities such as "3/5"); the label sits beside the middle of the edge, on its outer side, and moves along the edge if it would touch a node or another label. edgeColor colours that edge and its label (to trace one path). With edge labels the default gaps grow (gapX 30, gapY 74); trees without them are drawn exactly as before.

spec.title: Two draws without replacement from 3 red, 2 blue
spec.caption: P(RR) = 3/5 · 2/4 = 6/20. Multiply along a path; the leaf notes add up to 1.

name: tree — unbalanced probability tree
note: Leaves can sit at different depths; note writes a small line under a node (here unused).

spec.title: Coin, then a die if heads
spec.caption: P(H and 3–6) = 1/2 · 2/3 = 1/3.

name: er — entities, attributes, an M:N relationship
note: Chen notation on a grid: grid: [110, 70] px per column / row (fractions and negatives are fine; the picture is cropped to what is drawn). entities: [{id, label (default the id), at: [column, row], weak, color}]. rels (relationships): [{id, label, at, ident, color, links}] where links are [{to, card, total, role, cardAt, via, elbow, arrow, color}] or the short form ["Entity", "N", "total"]. attrs: [{of (an entity, relationship or attribute id), label, at, id (only needed when other attributes hang off it: a composite attribute), key (underlined), partial (dashed underline), multi (double oval), derived (dashed oval), color, via, elbow}]. total: true draws the double line of total participation. card is any text (1, N, M, (0,N), 1..*), set beside the line near the entity end and clear of every shape (cardAt: 0–1 along the line from the diamond fixes it). Entities are tinted a, relationships c, attributes plain unless color is given.

spec.title: Students enrol in courses
spec.caption: roll and code are keys; name is composite, phone multivalued, age derived; every student enrols (double line).

name: er — weak entity and identifying relationship
note: weak: true draws the double rectangle, ident: true the double diamond of the identifying relationship, partial: true the dashed underline of the partial key (discriminator). The weak entity's participation is total ("total" in the short link form).

spec.title: Dependants of an employee
spec.caption: A dependant is identified by (eid, dname).

name: er — specialisation: disjoint, total (circle)
note: isa: [{at, super (entity id), subs: [entity ids], kind: "d" (disjoint) | "o" (overlapping) | any short text such as "U", total: true (double line from the superclass), shape: "circle" (default) | "triangle", label (default the kind letter; ISA for a triangle), color}]. Subclass lines run from the circle to each subclass.

spec.title: Every person is a student or a faculty member, not both

name: er — ISA triangle, overlapping, partial
note: shape: "triangle" draws the ISA triangle (Korth); its apex turns towards the superclass and subclasses hang from its base. kind writes disjoint / overlapping beside it; without total the line from the superclass is single (partial specialisation).

name: er — aggregation
note: aggregations: [{id, around: [ids of a relationship and its entities], label, pad (default 12), color}] draw a dashed box round them; another relationship links to the box by its id, like an entity.

spec.title: A manager monitors (employee works on project)

name: er — recursive relationship with roles and (min,max)
note: via: [[column, row], …] bends a line through those points (right angles when neighbouring points share a row or column); elbow: "hv" (across, then up or down) or "vh" adds one corner. role writes a role name in italics beside the line; (min,max) pairs are just card text.

name: er — arrows for one, elbow connectors
note: arrow: true ends a link in an arrowhead at the entity (Korth: the arrow points to the "one" side). elbow: "vh" / "hv" routes a link or an attribute line with one right-angle corner.

spec.title: Each instructor belongs to one department

name: plot — vectors and arrows on a curve
note: A series with arrow: true (or "start" / "both") ends in an arrowhead. vectors: [{from (default [0,0]), to, label, color, dash}] draws single arrows in data coordinates (pos places the label: "above", "below", "left", "right") — gradients, displacements, eigenvectors. dash: true (or style: "dashed") dashes a series; legend: false on a series keeps it out of the legend; the diagram's legend takes "top-left" (default), "top-right", "bottom-left", "bottom-right", "outside" or "none".

spec.title: Vector addition
spec.caption: u = (4, 1), v = (1, 3); the dashed copy of v shows the parallelogram.

name: plot — hollow markers for a piecewise function
note: points: [{x, y, label, pos: "above" | "below" | "left" | "right", open: true, color}]. open: true draws a hollow marker — the value the function does not take at a jump. A series takes dots: true (filled) or dots: "open" to mark each of its own points; clip: true keeps every curve inside the plot box.

spec.title: A jump at x = 2
spec.caption: The hollow circle is not a value of f; the filled one is.

name: plot — log-log axes (growth rates)
note: xlog / ylog give a logarithmic axis: 2, 10 or true (= 10). The range must be positive. Tick labels are the powers of the base ($10^{6}$ beyond a few digits), and gridlines are drawn at each power; xticks / yticks still override them; clip: true cuts the curves at the box. Straight lines on log-log paper are power laws; a straight line on a log y axis alone is exponential growth.

spec.title: n, n log n, n² and 2ⁿ on log-log axes
spec.caption: Each power of n is a straight line; 2ⁿ leaves the box before n = 30.

name: graph — self-loops on any side
note: loop on a node ("above" default, "below", "left", "right") places every self-loop of that node; loop on an edge overrides it for that loop. Left and right loops put their label just past the curve. Other keys as in the DFA example: nodes x, y, shape double, start; edges from, to, label, curve.

spec.title: Binary numbers divisible by 3
spec.caption: State rk: the bits read so far leave remainder k. Reading bit b turns k into 2k + b (mod 3).

name: graph — a self-loop steps aside for an edge label
note: With no loop key a self-loop sits above its node, unless that would cover another edge's label: then it takes the side (below, right, left) that clears the labels, the other nodes and loops and the figure edge, crossing the fewest lines.

spec.title: Control-flow graph of a nested loop
spec.caption: The back edge B4 → B2 and its label run over B3, so B3's loop goes underneath.

name: tree — multi-line labels and maths in labels
note:
A label with 
 is set on several lines in a rounded box; levels move apart to fit the tallest box. Text between $...$ in any SVG label (every type) gets sub/superscripts and symbols: x_1, 2^{n}, \overline{x}, x', \alpha … \omega, \varepsilon, \le, \ge, 
e, 	o, \cdot, 	imes, \infty, \emptyset, \in, \cup, \cap, 
eg, \land, \lor, \oplus, \equiv, 
ot\equiv. A $ right after a letter or digit (a#b$c, $t0) stays a dollar sign. Keys as in the other tree examples: root, children, label, note, hl, highlight, color, r, gapX, gapY.

spec.title: Recursion tree of $T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n$
spec.caption: Every level costs n in total, and there are log₂ n + 1 levels: Θ(n log n).

name: tree — a lone child sits to its side (binary)
note: binary: true reads children as [left, right]; null marks a missing child. A node with exactly one child keeps an empty slot as wide as a leaf for the missing one, so the lone child sits clearly to the left or right. gap (px) sets that slot's width (the old look was gap = r).

spec.title: BST after inserting 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 80, 35
spec.caption: 35 is the left child of 40; 80 is the right child of 70.

name: gantt — long lane names
note: With lanes: "by-process", lane names longer than about 8 characters widen the left margin by themselves (short names keep the usual 64 px). Keys: blocks [{p, from, to, label}], lanes, axis {min, max, step}, marks [{t, label}], arrivals, queue, colors, w.

name: flow — decision questions of any length
note: A decision diamond grows until its text keeps a margin from the edges; a question longer than about 22 characters is set on two lines (split outside brackets and maths), or write your own \n. Keys: nodes [{id, label, kind: process | decision | start | end | io, color}], edges [[from, to, label]] or {from, to, label}, gapY, w.

nodes.label: Can a DFA with finitely many states decide it?
Does the pumping lemma fail for some $p$?

name: graph — maths in labels (ε-NFA)
note: Node and edge labels with $...$: $q_0$, $\varepsilon$, $a, b$. Plain labels are drawn exactly as before.

spec.title: An ε-NFA for $a^*b$
spec.caption: The dashed loop is only there to show a symbol on a right-hand loop.

name: nest — block scopes in C (static scoping)
note: root: a box {id, title, note, lines, rows, children, dir, color, hl, dash, mono}; lines are mono text (mono: false on a box sets them in the ordinary font; a string, or {t, hl, color} to mark one line); rows are [key, value] pairs (or {k, v, hl}). dir "h" puts a box's children side by side (default "v": stacked). Colours a-h (default: by depth). arrows [{from, to, label, side: "right" | "left", straight, color, dash}]: from / to are box ids, or "id.2" for the 2nd line or row of a box. Side arrows run round the margin; straight ones join the facing edges. Top level: root (or boxes, a list of boxes with no frame), dir (default for every box), highlight (box ids), w (minimum width), title, caption.

spec.title: Which x does the block use?
spec.caption: Name lookup walks outwards from the innermost block: y = 3, while main returns the global x = 1.

name: nest — call stack with static and dynamic links
note: boxes (instead of root) lists top-level boxes with no frame round them. A box id or "id.n" anchors an arrow; arrows on the same side get their own lanes. hl marks the running frame.

spec.title: Static vs dynamic scoping: main calls g, g calls f
spec.caption: Static scoping follows f's definition (globals) and prints 10; dynamic scoping follows the caller and prints 20.

name: nest — memory segments of a process
note: A note sits at the right of the title bar (addresses, sizes). rows align their values in one column.

name: nest — set containment (Chomsky hierarchy)
note: Nested boxes as a containment picture when circles would not fit: each box lies inside its superset. mono: false (set on every box here) uses the ordinary font for lines and notes; titles and lines may use $maths$.

spec.title: Every class lies inside the one around it

name: plot — break-even chart (CA)
note: Sales and total cost lines from their formulas; points mark the BEP. Ticks of 10,000 and above use Indian grouping (10,00,000) automatically; the left margin grows to fit them. Give your own xticks / yticks as [value, "label"] pairs for lakh labels.

spec.title: Tapri premix: break-even chart
spec.caption: Contribution ₹40 a box pays the ₹2,00,000 fixed cost at 5,000 boxes.

name: tree — variance tree (CA)
note: A tree with notes under nodes: the total variance splits into its parts; color marks Fav (ok) and Adv (bad) - say so in the caption, never by colour alone.

spec.title: Material cost variance
spec.caption: Green: favourable (F); rose: adverse (A). Each pair of children adds up to its parent.

name: table — cost sheet format (CA)
note: An ICAI pro-forma as a table: align sets each column's alignment (amounts right); cells colours cells (here the subtotal rows, hl). For formats in running text a markdown table (| … |, ---: right-aligns) is usually simpler; use this spec inside labs, folds and answers.

name: flow — audit opinion decision (CA)
note: Decisions with yes/no edges; end nodes coloured by outcome. Long questions wrap on two lines by themselves.

name: seq — communications with those charged with governance (CA)
note: Lanes are the parties; arrows are communications in order; a box on a lane is something a party does.

name: layers — strategy levels (CA)
note: Top to bottom; note and right give a second and third column.

layers.label: Business level
layers.note: how to compete in one business
